deliverable: Canonical online fused MLA as a SINGLE MixedKernel launch: QK with nope-panel accumulation and rope added once, right-aligned causal mask, GQA head mapping, online softmax in FP32, P conversion/pack, PV, normalize and output conversion. No full scores or P materialised in GM. Verified on Ascend950PR against all 20 official cases with the original comparator.

official_20_case_sweep.comparator: cannbench_contract.Harness + npu_compare.compare_case_result, ORIGINAL thresholds, warm fp64 oracle cache
official_20_case_sweep.shape_coverage: BSND and BNSD; D_nope 512 and 448; D_rope 64; float16 and bfloat16; causal and non-causal; prefill, cross (S>Skv, non-causal), long prefill, decode (S=1, Skv 2048/4096), MTP (S=2), large batch up to B=128.

layout_addressing.mechanism: as_strided pure-metadata views; the kernel is compiled against concrete strides and both layouts address the same bytes
layout_addressing.spec_clause: cases/mla.md 1: the host selects an implementation, validates metadata, allocates the output and launches only; no host concatenation, no whole-tensor transpose, no host softmax or matmul. Contiguous BSND/BNSD is reached directly by address mapping.
layout_addressing.why_not_a_transpose: a host .transpose().contiguous() would be a data movement and is forbidden; and it would not even be needed, since both layouts are the same bytes

semantics.rope_added_once: score = scale * (dot(q_nope,k_nope) + dot(q_rope,k_rope)); the rope GEMM is one additional clear_accum=False accumulation after the nope panels
semantics.causal: j <= i + (Skv - S), RIGHT-ALIGNED, applied as a vector compare against the block base offset
semantics.gqa: hkv = hq // G, reached by stride so the group axis costs no copy
semantics.scale: scaleValue <= 0 means 1/sqrt(D_qk) with D_qk = D_nope + D_rope, NOT D_v
semantics.v_contract: v == k_nope is a VALUE contract; the kernel reads the k_nope tile and makes no assumption about pointer aliasing
semantics.all_masked_rows: the golden zeroes a fully-masked row; the kernel's final normalize uses the running denominator, and a zero denominator is guarded

defects_found_and_fixed.why_dangerous: silent: no error and no NaN, just a different operator; 448 is official cases 3, 6, 14
defects_found_and_fixed.fix: panels derived from D with an explicit divisibility check

defects_found_and_fixed.symptom: NameError: name batch is not defined
defects_found_and_fixed.cause: from __future__ import annotations stringifies prim_func annotations and TileLang resolves them with get_type_hints() in the closure scope
defects_found_and_fixed.fix: removed, with a comment so a linter does not restore it

defects_found_and_fixed.symptom: ABI asserted an impossible stride (expected 65536, got 51)
defects_found_and_fixed.cause: declared rank-5 StridedTensors but passed rank-4 tensors, so the ABI read past the end of the runtime stride array; every BSND case passed by coincidence because rank-4 BSND strides equal the leading four of the rank-5 view

defects_found_and_fixed.symptom: a BNSD call reused a BSND-compiled kernel
defects_found_and_fixed.why_dangerous: the strides are a compile-time specialization; a compatible-looking stride set would have read the right number of elements from the WRONG POSITIONS
defects_found_and_fixed.fix: layout is part of the key

my_own_test_bugs_recorded: the first three device runs reported failure because MY harness passed an independent random v while both kernels use k_nope as V. The fixture get_input() replaces v with a copy of k_nope for exactly this reason. Proven, not assumed: running the WORKING reference through my own harness reproduced my kernel exact numbers.

before that, two CPU algebra harnesses reported 20/20 failures -- one measuring fp16/bf16 storage rounding, one whose round-trip was a no-op. Only comparing an fp64 golden against an fp64 recomputation made the sides comparable; then all 20 agreed to ~3e-8.
I also corrupted kernel.py with a bad string slice (it grew to 792 lines with duplicated content) and caught it only because the syntax check failed before commit.
not_claimed: No performance claim: no cycle timings, no bandwidth figure, no comparison against any baseline kernel. This gate is numerical correctness and single-launch structure only.
A fully-masked row is checked by rule and by the golden zeroing convention, not executed as a dedicated device case.
Physical synchronisation equivalence is not proven: the pipeline stages and buffer versions are what the compiler emitted, not an argument about hardware event ordering.
The BNSD path shares one compiled kernel per shape; it is not separately timed.
